clue.text: North's devious ending of the royal supporter

indicators.note: devious means winding or crooked, so the letters of North take an indirect new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, here taken from the

explanation.surface: A northern courtier's crooked plot brings an end to the king's loyal backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devious' rearranges NORTH (the possessive 's adds no letter) to THRON, and 'ending of' takes E from 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's chair of state literally holds up the sovereign, a playful way to name the seat.

clue.text: Bottle each overcome sorrow

parts.note: bottle is British slang for courage or nerve, as is heart

indicators.note: overcome suggests the word each is overwhelmed and thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Each person drowning their sorrow with a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' looks like drink, but it is British slang for nerve. 'overcome' rearranges EACH to ACHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotional pain or grief is a synonym for deep sadness.

clue.text: Where the cargo space hatch is waiting to be connected?

definitions.text: Where the cargo space hatch is
definitions.meaning: a hatch sits on the hold, the cargo compartment of a ship
a telephone caller kept waiting for the line to go through

explanation.surface: A ship's hatch and a caller left hanging on the phone line.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatch is set on top of a ship's hold; a telephone caller left waiting is said to be kept suspended this way.

clue.text: Doubled up three times out of delight

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of of and delight are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone bent double three times over, convulsed with joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges OF and DELIGHT together into the nine-letter answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubling three times multiplies by two cubed, so the result is multiplied by a factor of eight.

clue.text: Sound of cow giving birth under a diner, perhaps

indicators.note: sound of tells us to say a word aloud and enter what it resembles

parts.note: a calver is a cow that calves, that is gives birth

explanation.surface: A cow lowing as it calves beneath someone eating dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent, CALVER and the answer sound alike. A carver is a dining chair with arms, so it sits under a diner.
explanation.definitionFit: A carver is an armed dining chair, an item of furniture that a person eating sits upon.

clue.text: Very sad, losing head and going up in smoke

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the letters are read from bottom to top, in reverse
losing head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: very sad means tragic

explanation.surface: Someone's hopes vanishing in smoke, leaving them miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops T from TRAGIC to leave RAGIC, which 'going up' turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoke is a casual word for something smoked, such as a rolled tobacco leaf.

clue.text: Hired demonstrators rude to barmen

indicators.note: rude here means rough or crude, signalling the letters of to barmen are roughly rearranged

explanation.surface: Paid protesters being rude to the staff behind the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rude' rearranges TO and BARMEN together.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowd of protesters paid to turn out is known by this British informal term.

clue.text: Strain: it really makes you sick

definitions.text: Strain: it really makes you sick

parts.words: Strain: it really makes you sick
parts.note: strain reads as stress, but here it is a strain of bacterium that causes food poisoning

explanation.surface: Stress at work is enough to make anyone ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain of a gut bacterium notorious for causing food poisoning, a microbial variety.

clue.text: Stomach 75% oversize? This will flatten it!

parts.note: to stomach something is to bear it

indicators.note: 75% keeps the first three of the four letters of a word meaning oversize

parts.note: oversize means huge

explanation.surface: A big belly about to be squashed by an enthusiastic embrace.
explanation.walkthrough: '75%' keeps the first three quarters of HUGE. The definition reads back to the whole clue: 'it' is the oversize stomach a squeeze would flatten.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight crushing embrace would squash anything in its way, such as a large belly.

clue.text: It combats angina flutter with a type of blood container

parts.note: flutter is British slang for a small wager
B is one of the blood groups
a locker is a storage container

explanation.surface: A heart treatment involves a racing pulse and a vessel full of blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flutter' suggests a heart palpitation, which suits the angina surface, but it is a small bet.
explanation.definitionFit: This class of drug slows the heart and is prescribed to relieve chest pain from angina.

clue.text: Crafty threat, during negotiations, of crumbling bun in butter

indicators.note: in places the scrambled letters inside the other word

parts.note: a butter is something that butts, such as a goat

indicators.note: crumbling means falling apart, so the letters of bun are broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: A recipe for a bun crumbled into butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' looks like the dairy spread but means a creature that butts, and 'Crafty' puns on a vessel. 'crumbling' rearranges BUN to UNB.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunboat diplomacy is the veiled threat of naval force while talks go on; 'crafty' puns on a craft, a vessel.

clue.text: Passionate, excited — toupee must start to slip!

indicators.note: excited means agitated, so the letters of toupee must are stirred up
the start of a word is its first letter, taken from slip

explanation.surface: A man anxiously hoping his hairpiece will not slide off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges TOUPEE and MUST, and 'start to' adds S from 'slip'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormy and full of strong emotion, so intensely ardent.

clue.text: Reckon sex allied to Nazi doctrine soundly sums up Stalin's way

parts.note: to reckon is to add up, to total
it is a dated euphemism for sex or sex appeal

indicators.note: soundly tells us to take a word by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: the Nazi doctrine of a master race was Aryanism

explanation.surface: A historian sums up Stalinism as sex tied to Nazi thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: ARIANISM, an early Christian heresy, sounds like ARYANISM. 'allied to' and 'sums up' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalin ruled the Soviet Union as a one-party state with absolute central control, the system named here.

clue.text: See 26
You could drive on it, whip round, then do point-to-point

indicators.note: round means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to whip is to flog
point-to-point is horse racing across country, and to course is to race or chase

explanation.surface: A jockey whips the horse round and then rides a cross-country race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' sounds like driving a car, but it is a long golf shot. A point-to-point is a British amateur horse race over farmland.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer drives from the tee, so this playing ground is somewhere you could hit a drive.

clue.text: Monetary vertical projection by party has Ali in a spin

parts.note: a fin is a vertical projection, as on a fish or an aircraft tail
the ANC, the African National Congress, is the South African political party

indicators.note: in a spin means whirling or confused, so the letters of Ali are turned about

explanation.surface: A party boxer named Ali is sent spinning by an upright blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a spin' rearranges ALI to IAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to money and its management, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Note rising up worktop's upright

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word up is read from the bottom, in reverse

parts.note: a table is a worktop; the possessive 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: A kitchen note says the worktop's upright stand is lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns UP into PU.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright in the moral sense, honest and respectable, matches well regarded and trustworthy.

clue.text: It never took off and now it has died out

definitions.text: It never took off and now it has died out

parts.words: It never took off and now it has died out
parts.note: reads like a failed product, but describes a flightless seabird hunted to extinction in the nineteenth century

explanation.surface: A business venture that never got going and has now folded.
explanation.definitionFit: This flightless North Atlantic seabird could never fly and was hunted to extinction by 1844.

clue.text: Principal recovered from the effects of county division

parts.note: to be over something is to have got over it
a riding was one of the three divisions of the county of Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A head teacher getting over a local boundary split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Principal' looks like a head teacher, but it is an adjective. A RIDING was one of three districts of Yorkshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Overriding means dominant, most important, just as a principal concern is the chief one.

clue.text: Second hit in a row

parts.note: to pat is to strike lightly

explanation.surface: Being struck twice in succession.
explanation.definitionFit: A short petty quarrel, an argument or squabble.

clue.text: Contrived detachment, perhaps, on date

parts.note: a detachment of soldiers is an example of a military force

explanation.surface: An aloof manner put on for a romantic evening out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detachment' suggests aloofness but means a body of troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unnatural and artificial, like a strained smile, is said to be contrived.

clue.text: Be acutely aware Ken has an obsession: to row at sea

parts.note: ken is a Scots and northern word meaning to know
to have a thing about something is to be obsessed with it

indicators.note: at sea means confused or in disarray, so the letters of to row are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man named Ken is obsessed with rowing on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ken' looks like a name but is the Scots verb. 'at sea' rearranges TO ROW to ORTWO.
explanation.definitionFit: To be well informed and experienced about something is an idiom for being sharply aware.

clue.text: Cap that's hardly fashionable at party

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: An unfashionable hat worn to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cap' looks like a hat but is the verb meaning to top or surpass.
explanation.definitionFit: To cap someone's story is to surpass it, beating it in a contest.

clue.text: Pedestrian type who makes president in short time

indicators.note: in places the president inside the shortened time

parts.note: hr is short for hour
Ike was the nickname of US President Eisenhower

explanation.surface: Someone dull who becomes a head of state within a brief spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedestrian' suggests dull, but here means one who goes on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler who walks in the countryside is one kind of walker, a person on foot.

clue.text: Snappy press gang getting Jack back on deck

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor, as is a tar
a deck of cards is a pack

explanation.surface: A naval press gang hauls a sailor back on board ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press gang' suggests naval recruiters, but means journalists; 'snappy' refers to photographers taking snaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used for a pack of paparazzi or tabloid reporters chasing celebrities with cameras.

clue.text: Sleepers quite taken by this trendy new reporter on the Guardian

parts.note: in means fashionable
a cub is a novice journalist
since the clue appears in the Guardian, the newspaper refers to itself as us

explanation.surface: A fashionable rookie journalist joins the Guardian.
explanation.walkthrough: An incubus is a demon said to lie upon and seduce sleeping women, so it takes sleepers. 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Folklore tells of a male demon that ravishes people in their sleep, so sleepers are quite literally taken by it.

clue.text: US TV series is after Stone — Mick Jagger?

parts.note: a stone is a rock
ER is the American hospital drama series

explanation.surface: A Rolling Stone star turns up in an American television show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is after' signals the order of the charade. 'Stone' points to the Rolling Stones, but simply means a large stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Jagger fronts a rock band, so he is an example of a rock musician.

clue.text: Chair needs council's tip on summer finance

indicators.note: the tip of a word here is its final letter, taken from council's

parts.note: a summer is one who sums, an adder
to back a project is to finance it

explanation.surface: A council leader wants a cut of the summer budget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' looks like the season but means one who adds up. 'needs' and 'on' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden chair whose back has horizontal slats like rungs is a traditional example of a seat.
